questions.q: Which cognitive ability do the authors call uniquely human and central to cooperation?
a: Understanding that others have knowledge and intentions of their own
The ability to copy sounds and gestures
The capacity to remember past events
The instinct to follow a strong leader
questions.why: Lesson 1 says this understanding, which even a nine-month-old shows, made cooperation possible.

questions.q: How did chimpanzees perform in the cup game?
a: They did not grasp that the researcher knew something they did not
They found the treat faster than dogs did
They learned the gesture and applied it to new ones
They ignored the cups and the researcher completely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says chimps only learn a specific gesture through repetition and fail when it changes.

questions.q: What did Belyaev's fox experiment demonstrate?
a: Selecting for friendliness brought physical and mental changes with it
Wild foxes could be tamed through training alone
Domestication made foxes worse at reading human gestures
Aggression was necessary for survival in captivity
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the friendlier foxes changed in body and became better at communicating with humans.

questions.q: Which physical changes appeared in the friendlier foxes?
a: Softer fur, shorter snouts and floppier ears
Larger teeth and longer snouts
Thicker coats and sharper claws
Darker eyes and stronger jaws
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists these traits as side effects of breeding for tameness, not traits chosen directly.

questions.q: Why do humans have visible whites in their eyes, according to the authors?
a: They help us tell whether someone is making eye contact
They shield the eye from bright sunlight
They signal health to potential mates
They widen our peripheral vision
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the white sclerae are a modern sign of how much we rely on social cues.
